response.meaning: answered — no flag stands; coverage INCOMPLETE — uncertified (coverage.refused_obligations names what was not judged)
response.report:
MANDATE: 1 group(s) over 2 lines, 1 mandated pair(s), source=declared (--groups=)
           group A = lines 1,2 — GRADED WHETHER OR NOT ANYTHING IS SAID ABOUT THEM BELOW; silence here is a clean group, not an unasked question (doctrine 20)
  BLUEPRINT: none declared — meter and song-function are NOT asked; only rhyme and the slop floor are (doctrine 20: this is a refusal on those two layers, not evidence they are clean)
  draft: 2 line(s), md5 7eac7ab2e852
  SCHEMA RELATIONS: 1 mandated pair(s) stand in at least one registry schema (every pair is judged against every schema, beside the coarse relations) — L1~L2 (group A): Scots vowel-length rhyme (Aitken's Law), assonance, cluster consonance / skothending span, consonance, enjambed rhyme, family rhyme, head rhyme (positional), linked rhyme, pantun ABAB, perfect rhyme — laziness at these relations is UNCALIBRATED; declaring a relation narrows
    of those, 1 read as END RHYME and 0 do NOT — two counts, never summed: a schema is the end-rhyme reading only when BOTH its spans sit at the line-final token and it requires the nucleus AND the coda to agree. The rest are real relations this grade judges correctly and a listener does not hear as the lines rhyming.
    (the schema family's chance rate is PINNED at 896..921 of 4,000 random CMUdict pairs (22.4%–23.0%, 5.7–5.8x the sonnet canon arm's 3.95%; quality/chance_rate.py, a band over its sampler grid) and UNPRICED)
  ADJACENCY: longest stress run 1 (L1), longest weak run 0 (L1) — disclosed, uncalibrated, never charged.
  REPORT: 1 line(s) briefed — 0 FLAG, 1 NOTE (two counts, never summed: doctrine 79); 1 WHOLE-DRAFT finding(s), 0 of them FLAG(S), below

  WHAT TO CHANGE — 0 decision(s). Flags only; the notes below are measurements handed back, not defects (doctrine 96)
    nothing on any line, and nothing about the draft as a whole, carries a flag. The notes below still say what the draft is doing

  THE EVIDENCE — every finding not rolled up, in full; the lines carrying an un-rolled flag first
  L2: hat
      FINDING [NOTE] HOMEOTELEUTON: L1/L2 rhyme on the SAME SPELLED ENDING ('cat'/'hat', both -at) — the laziest class, banned before any frequency judgment (lines 1, 2)
         spelled rime 'at' on both sides. The near relations the taxonomy names (declared via Declaration.admit) are the palette that keeps this ban from closing the class: reach for a differently-spelled partner or a declared near rhyme, not the next word in the same spelling family.
      must answer group A [1, 2]: L1 ('cat') — HOLDS, but carries NOTE HOMEOTELEUTON, which the loop still asks to change
      FORBIDDEN (modal — doctrine 9): that, at, sat, spat, fat, flat, mat, rat, chat, what, hat, bat, pat, somewhat, brat, kat, nat, swat, twat, stat, dat, tat, vat, scat, wat, splat, lat, gat, begat, gnat, sadat, nonfat, gujarat
      ALREADY THERE (a different rule — re-proposing the end word that is already on this line is not a revision): hat
      offered: matt, pratt, habitat, diplomat, pussycat, democrat, copycat, format, aristocrat, chitchat, laundromat, wildcat

  WHOLE DRAFT — 1 finding(s) that name no single line, 0 of them FLAG(S)
      These findings measure the complete draft or its declarations and assign no single target line. A permitted local edit can improve a text-dependent finding, and the declared whole-draft writer can be asked for a wider repair. `verify()` reads these findings alongside per-line findings. Rewriting words cannot repair an unchanged grid declaration.
      FINDING [NOTE] OUT_OF_CALIBRATED_LENGTH: 2 tokens is outside every calibrated length; the length-sensitive checks did not run
         profiles cover section 28-36 (reach 14-72), sonnet 105-123 (reach 52-246), lyric 4-3244 (reach 4-3244) tokens, each with its own declared reach. MATTR in particular is a moving average over a 50-token window (declared: FloorDeclaration.mattr_window) and silently degrades to plain type-token ratio below that, so a threshold measured at one length is a different statistic at another. WHAT DID RUN: the relation-level checks (self-rhyme, radif, cliche, shared suffix), which read no percentile and do not depend on length. Of those, only REPEAT_IN_VERSE can still be a FLAG here — a word rhymed with itself is a fact about the two lines and needs no calibration. CLICHE_PAIR is a NOTE at this length: nothing about the membership test changes, but the only false-positive rates it has were measured in the two SUPERSEDED band rows — 7.33% at 150-350 tokens (`song`, seed 5th-95th 5.69-8.71%) and 4.51% at 50-150 tokens (`short`, seed 5th-95th 3.96-5.08%) — and neither covers 2 tokens. REPINNED 2026-09-05: this branch used to add that out here the check runs at 14.74% against 6.35% in band (285 corpus items, 42 firing); that 285-item population was the corpus outside the 2026-08-14 BAND table, and under the live table it is empty — no corpus item sits under 4 or over 3,245 tokens, so there is no measured rate out here at all (doctrine 22), which is exactly why this is a note. RADIF_LICENSED and SHARED_SUFFIX are notes at every length
